learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of soft skills, i.e. those skills that are not strictly technical, but which nevertheless constitute an indispensable asset for success in the world of work
Knowledge and understanding of the structure and forms of technical-scientific literature
Knowledge and understanding of the epochal changes of the information society in the technological, economic and legislative fields.
Identifying one's own strengths and weaknesses in the field of soft skills
Identifying the essential components of a scientific article
Identifying the mutual influences between information technology and society
Ability to critically discuss the role of soft skills in the profession and in recruitment processes
Ability to analyze and critically discuss the preponderant role that scientific publication is having in the development of science and in the careers of engineers and scientists
Ability to analyze and critically discuss the opportunities and risks of the information society
Ability to effectively present one's ideas in an open teacher-student discussion
Ability to independently find information and texts on the topics covered

syllabus_topics: Soft skills as added value in the world of work.
The information society and related technologies.
Why technical skills (hard skills) are not enough.
Trust in people and the context (optimism)
Corpus of acquired knowledge and paradigms
Criteria for accepting a publication scientific
The “canonical” structure of a scientific publication
Introduction to the concept of "Information Society" (Hypercommunication): economic, social and technological aspects.
Historical and technological evolution of the Internet and Web2.0.
Analysis of the main Social Networks and the economic paradigm of Big Data.
Examination of technical documents (e.g., RFCs) related to the management of HTTP cookies and PUSH notifications.
Concept and regulation of privacy in the perspective of control, surveillance and censorship: Web content search engines.
Role of the Guarantor and European reference legislation: GDPR.
Concept of IT security, related crimes (e.g., phishing, fraud), legislation and examinations of some cases (Social Network down, DDOS, redirect).

assessment_methods.method: Quizzes administered at the end of class (V3)

assessment_rules: The final grade is the weighted sum of the three grades: V = 0.35 * V1 + 0.05 * V2 + 0.6 * V3, where each item is graded between 0 and 1. A passing grade is 0.6. The final grade is expressed as: excellent, distinguished, good, fair, or sufficient. Even those who do not attend class can still achieve a passing grade if they obtain the maximum score (100%) on the final quiz.
